finding.comment: files_jsonl contains one object per line, but the consumer iterates .[] as if it held a single array; on each per-line object .[] walks the object's own values, so the textual-changes check misreads the documented format.

files.patch:
--- a/scripts/collect.sh
+++ b/scripts/collect.sh
@@ -1,3 +1,4 @@
 # changed files were gathered as JSONL (one object per line):
 #   jq -c '.[]' <<<"$batch" >>"$files_jsonl"
+jq '.[] | select(.patch != null)' <"$files_jsonl" >/dev/null
+echo "textual changes present"
